title: Check the Bag
cues: Every October, some mama dumps the pillowcase out on the kitchen table
Dim kitchen, a single pillowcase sprawled on a scarred wood table, grey light
intro_or_break
And goes through it. Piece by piece
Close-up hands meticulously sorting through a crumpled, dark cloth
intro_or_break
I'm the piece she's lookin' for
A shadowed figure, back turned, searching intently within the darkness
intro_or_break
Nineteen sixty-somethin', a newspaper wrote me down
Vintage newspaper clipping floats in a hazy, sepia-toned room, distorted
drive
Didn't print a face, didn't need one, I was all over town
Silhouetted figures darting through a rain-slicked, urban alleyway, blurred motion
drive
Razor in the apple, needle in the chocolate bar
A gleaming apple with a shard of glass embedded in its skin, dark chocolate
drive
Fifty years of headlines and I never left a scar
Pale, aged parchment scrolls with shadowy script, aged and brittle
drive
Never rang a doorbell, never cut across a yard
Empty doorway, receding into a dark, overgrown garden, stillness
drive
Never touched a single bowl, and every mama's on her guard
Hands carefully avoiding a porcelain bowl, a sense of unease
drive
Hospitals X-ray the candy on the thirty-first for free
X-ray images of brightly colored candy rotating slowly in a sterile room
drive

A long, winding line of dark figures waiting, shrouded in shadows
drive

Abandoned popcorn kernels scattered across a bleak, grey countertop
drive

A dark, overflowing garbage bin, a sticky, melted chocolate residue
drive
Fifty years I never happened, and you still check the bag
A single, heavy bag sits on a worn kitchen table, illuminated by a single bulb
drive
Dump it on the kitchen table, every wrapper, every tag
A chaotic pile of paper remnants and twisted wrapping – frantic, close up
drive
I don't lift a finger, and I still get paid in dread
A porch light flickers erratically, casting grotesque shadows on the street
drive
Every porch light in the country burnin' off of what they said
Multiple porch lights burn intensely, casting a wide, unsettling glow
drive
You moved trick-or-treat to a parkin' lot at four
Children in plastic capes quickly walk between darkened vans in a row
drive
Daylight in a church van 'cause you couldn't trust a door
A parked church van with tinted windows, rain streaks across the glass
drive
Kids in plastic capes walkin' trunk to trunk in pairs
Dark figures in plastic capes pass quickly, a sense of urgency and fear
drive
That's a whole tradition I rewrote, and I was never there
Dim, fractured city skyline reflected in a rain-slicked window
drive
Ask a cop for one real case and watch him study his shoes
A lone police officer’s silhouette, head bowed, examining worn shoes
drive
Every story is a cousin's friend who saw it on the news
Blurred, shadowy figures watching a news screen from a distance
drive
I'm a rumor with a rap sheet and a mugshot with no face
A grainy, black and white mugshot with a faceless, distorted hand
drive
You can't cuff a story, so the story runs the place
A swirling vortex of dark smoke and fractured reflections
drive
I ain't never had a body, and I'm workin' every year
An antique clock ticking slowly in a darkened, dusty room
drive
Scariest man in America, and I was never here
A colossal, shifting silhouette looms over a desolate landscape
drive
I was never here
Reverse shot of a single, dark hand reaching out from shadows
drive
I was never here
Reverse shot of a single, dark hand reaching out from shadows
drive

A jeweler's loupe focuses on a glistening, translucent caramel
drive

drive
